entries.subject: DRAFT-device job admission contradicts FROZEN F4/F6/F7/F12 (StepExecutor/JobAdmissionService/DeviceStatePort) enforcement
entries.text:
CONTRACT CONTRADICTION -- STOPPING BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION (per this packet's own requirement: "If a contract clause and this packet disagree, raise a RELAY_QUESTION and STOP; never reconcile silently and never relax a direction test").

This movement's objective is: POST /devices/add-single creates the DRAFT device row and admits a C2 confirm job against it; a worker claims that job and contacts the device; on success the row lands ENROLLED with the observed facts.

The already-merged B1-4/B1-4b code enforces the opposite rule at four independent, tested points, all tied to FROZEN adjudications F4/F6/F7/F12:

1. JobAdmissionService.submit() (job-engine/.../admission/JobAdmissionService.java lines 68-80): refuses admission with DEVICE_NOT_ELIGIBLE for any device whose enrollment_state does not permit read collection -- comment: "does not permit a job to be created against it (DRAFT is refused here)".
2. DeviceEnrollmentState.permitsReadCollection() (platform-core, DeviceEnrollmentState.java): "Contract Section 3: DRAFT never permits collection or a job."
3. StepExecutor.execute() (job-engine/.../executor/StepExecutor.java lines 100-109): re-checks enrollment at claim time and returns JobOutcome.Rejected("DEVICE_NOT_ELIGIBLE_AT_CLAIM_TIME") before EXECUTING, before any device contact -- covered by its own regression test, DraftDeviceRefusedAtClaimTimeTest, which asserts "a DRAFT device at claim time must never be contacted."
4. JooqDeviceStatePort.recordContactOutcome() / DeviceStatePort javadoc (persistence + platform-core): a DRAFT device is refused with DRAFT_DEVICE_NOT_CONTACTABLE -- "a DRAFT device is confirmed via the enrollment-confirm action, never a contact outcome... this movement's own registration flow never hands a DRAFT device to an executor in the first place."

All four say, with test coverage, that a DRAFT device is never admitted into a job and never handed to an executor/worker for contact; DRAFT -> ENROLLED must happen through a separate, already-anticipated "enrollment-confirm action" that is not a job/worker contact outcome.

This movement's brief requires exactly the path those four points refuse: admit a C2 job whose target is the new DRAFT device, and have the worker's StepExecutor contact it and land it ENROLLED. Implementing this as specified would require weakening JobAdmissionService's or StepExecutor's DRAFT refusal (an explicitly forbidden direction-rule relaxation per this movement's own "Files you must not touch": "Relaxing ... any direction rule"), or inventing a second admission/execution path that bypasses the existing gate (a silent reconciliation, also forbidden). Neither is available under this brief's own constraints.

I have not modified JobAdmissionService, StepExecutor, DeviceEnrollmentState, DeviceStatePort, or any migration, and have made no other repository changes this session.

QUESTION FOR THE PRODUCT OWNER: which authority yields? Concretely, is the intended design:
(a) the confirm job's admission and claim-time check are meant to treat DRAFT as eligible specifically for the confirm capability (an explicit, narrow amendment to F4/F6, naming exactly which capability/action-class is exempt and why disabled/deleted devices still refuse), or
(b) DRAFT -> ENROLLED is meant to go through the "separate, authorized confirm action" that JooqDeviceStatePort's comment already anticipates -- i.e. the confirm job's completion handler writes facts and calls a dedicated confirm-transition write (not JobAdmissionService/StepExecutor's generic device-eligibility gate at all), meaning admission for this one job type needs a different eligibility predicate than "permitsReadCollection" -- and if so, exactly what that predicate is (DRAFT permitted, still refusing disabled/deleted), or
(c) something else this packet has not named.

Awaiting a RELAY_DECISION or RELAY_CORRECTION before any implementation proceeds. No code was changed.

entries.subject: Resolved: the confirm is the one job kind admissible against DRAFT; every other kind keeps F4's refusal
entries.text: Right call to stop. The contradiction is real and is resolved by a recorded successor clause, not by reading one side away: EC-J1 exactly one job kind -- the enrollment confirm, whose capability is the closed four-read set -- is admissible against a DRAFT device; EC-J2 every other job kind keeps F4's refusal at all four enforcement points (JobAdmissionService, DeviceEnrollmentState.permitsReadCollection stays false for DRAFT, StepExecutor claim-time check, DeviceStatePort), and a test proves both sides; EC-J3 the confirm job's completion moves the row DRAFT -> ENROLLED (EC-6a on mismatch); EC-J4 the confirm job obeys every C2 rule in full; EC-J5 peer follow runs inside the same job. Implement by distinguishing the confirm job kind at those four points -- never by widening permitsReadCollection or by an execution path outside C2/C4. The packet's objective stands otherwise. Proceed from a fresh dispatch: your worktree will be recreated from origin/main once the record is merged.
